utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do receive a language I like very much, but on a channel -- channel 4, I received French. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see we have a videolink with the undue at this moment. Dr. Eekhof, can you see me? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: Yes, I can see you; I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I don't see and hear you. Yes. Yes, I would like to ask you again whether you can see me, whether you can hear me.

utterances.speaker: DR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: I can see and I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We also now can hear you, if we are plugged in on the right socket. Before we start, could the Simatovic Defence -- I would say the new Simatovic Defence introduce itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to the colleagues from the OTP. I'm attorney at law, Bakrac, and I am the newly appointed Defence counsel for Mr. Simatovic. And Ms. Ingrid Morgan is today with me in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome in this courtroom, Mr. Bakrac. We'll come to the newly appointed Simatovic Defence in a minute. I see that the Stanisic Defence is present, and the Prosecution is present. I'd first like to already ask right from the beginning whether there are any questions for Dr. Eekhof either from Prosecution side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Knoops, any question for Dr. Eekhof?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour, for Dr. Eekhof. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I started with this, Dr. Eekhof, because I didn't want to keep you busy for any minute longer than necessary. Just for your information the Chamber always tries once the documents are received to inquire with the parties whether they have any questions for you. Now, sometimes it is not easy to communicate with the parties, and that can result now and then, unfortunately, in you being present, although no questions for -- to be put to you at this moment. So therefore, as far as I'm concerned, you are excused. We've received - and I'll put that on the record - we've received your report from this morning. We have received the last weekly report. We have received the absence from court due to illness form, and we have received the short form undue medical service questions which were signed by you as well. We've received them. We also received the Jovica Stanisic non-attendance in court form. There are no questions for you, we have received all the written documents. Thank you very much for making yourself available, and we'll try to avoid that you have to be in the videolink if there are no questions for you.

utterances.speaker: DR. EEKHOF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, but it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you are excused. Any party would like to make any observations as far as continuing the proceedings in what appears to be the absence of Mr. Stanisic? MR. Knoops?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: No comment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Knoops, I take it that you have -- we have received the report of the reporting psychiatrist Dr. De Man, you've received that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I ask you this because you had expressed specific wishes in relation to the reporting by the psychiatrist. Any other matter in relation to Mr. Stanisic's health to be raised at this moment? If not, we'll proceed in the absence of Mr. Stanisic. The Chamber received a decision by the Deputy Registrar, dated the 11th of September of this year, in which it is decided that Mr. Bakrac is assigned as counsel to the accused Simatovic, effective from the 11th of September. The withdrawal of the assignment of Mr. Domazet and assignment of Mr. Petrovic as co-counsel to Mr. Bakrac, effective also the 11th of September, 2009. And finally in this decision, Mr. Domazet is directed to hand over to Mr. Bakrac any case related materials he received or produced during his assignment in accordance with his duties under Article 9(d) of the code of conduct, and to cooperate with the newly constituted Defence team for the period of his assignment as legal consultant. Any matters to be raised in relation to this decision by the Registry? No questions in relation to that. Then, I would like to -- before we move on to two motions that have been recently filed, the Chamber would like to give its guidance on the issue of exhibit stamps which was raised during one of the -- the testimony of one of the witnesses. It's, therefore, now the Chamber's instructions on the issue of exhibit stamps will be read by me. During the hearing of the 27th of August 2009, the issue of the presence of trace markings from other cases on documents sought for admission in the present case arose. The Prosecution suggested that ordinary documents tendered in this case should be differentiated from documents which are sought for admission as part of a Rule 92 ter package. The Chamber informed the parties that it would further consider this matter and having done so, the Chamber's position is as follows: For documents which are tendered as written evidence from another case in application of rules 92 bis, 92 ter, or 92 quater, the Chamber agrees that it would be useful for these documents to bear the trace markings received in those other cases, if there are any. In such instance, the party tendering the documents would not have to present in addition a clean copy of the document. For all other documents, however, the Chamber wishes to avoid unnecessary markings on the documents sought for admission which originate from the documents processing as evidence in other cases. In such instance, the party tendering the document would have to present a copy of the document without the trace markings that may have been placed in other trial proceedings. This concludes the Chamber's instruction. Perhaps I could add that of course even if we find no traces of the way in which these documents were processed in other cases as evidence, of course we find often additional markings such as stamps on -- in which the authenticity of the document is confirmed or we have ERN numbers, and that's not what this guidance is about. It's just about exhibit numbers in other cases. So admission into evidence, these kind of markings that come from other cases, again to be accepted if the document is tendered specifically as a document which was used in the other case and otherwise not to be found on it. Any questions in relation to this? No questions. Then the Chamber has received recently, not to say very recently, two motions by the Simatovic Defence of the 14th of December. The first Defence motion requesting adjournment of trial proceedings; and the other one, Defence motion requesting provisional release of Mr. Simatovic. The Prosecution, as usually, will have two weeks to respond to these motions. There will be no hearings until a decision on these motions has been delivered. Mr. Knoops, is it the intent of the Stanisic Defence to respond to these motions as well, or would you still consider your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for asking me this question. The position of the Stanisic Defence is that we will leave it into the hands of the Court with respect to the motion for adjournment of proceedings on the request of Mr. Simatovic. With respect to the provisional release, we think that in terms of judicial economy, it's wise to announce the Chamber that also considering these developments, that the Stanisic Defence will file in due course a similar motion for provisional release. Maybe that could be taken into account with respect to the responses of the Prosecution and the Chamber's decision, and then hopefully we are able to file that motion in due course. We anticipate to file this motion maybe this week. So that's the -- Prosecution could respond maybe to both applications at the same time, and the Court can render the decision on the both requests for provisional release at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Simultaneously, yes. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just received Mr. Simatovic's provisional release application before coming to Court; I haven't had a chance to study it. But it seems that both of them would be conditioned upon the Chamber's decision with respect to an adjournment. So if with the Court's leave, the Prosecution would respond to those, conditionally, that should the Chamber decide that an adjournment is appropriate here, that that would be our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some adjournment already of course is decided because we will not hear the case until we have decided on these motions. So that is already an inherent adjournment. But you'd say the adjournment as requested by the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And then, Your Honour, I had come prepared today - I welcomed the Chamber's opportunity to respond in writing - but I had come today prepared to make some submissions to the Court with respect to the motion for adjournment, so just to correct some factual matters in the motion if the Chamber is assisted by that. And also had some observations to make, submissions to the Chamber to make, should there be an adjournment, how -- some suggestions for how we might make productive time or use of that time so that when we do resume active hearings, that we can expedite matters before the Chamber. I can put that in a written form if the Chamber would prefer in the response to the motion for adjournment, or I'm happy to discuss some of those today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, if there are any corrections to be made in relation to factual information contained in the motions, then the Chamber would like to hear it now, which would also result in the Simatovic Defence hearing it and even being to able correct, if there's any need for that, its motion, or to further explain those matters so that we can take them all together when we finally will decide on the motions. Apart from that, so what your position would be that that -- the Chamber will be glad to receive that in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just the two factual corrections are - I think it was paragraph 11 of the application - it stated that the Prosecution exhibit list was of -- had 5.000 exhibits. The actual number of exhibits is 3.548, and I think in the same paragraph, it was stated that the Prosecution intended to call over 100 witnesses. There are 100 witnesses, 64 of which would be called for hearings. So there is a substantial number that would not be called live. And it may the Chamber as well, I asked for a calculation of the amount of materials for the first five witnesses. And for the first five witnesses, Your Honour, the number -- the amount of material that we would be dealing with would be 112 exhibits, 7 statements, 11 days of prior testimony, and 6 proofing notes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and those were the first five witnesses already scheduled, or now being scheduled to accommodate the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the best way to consider that is kind of a random sample from the witness list. Because until we know an actual date of hearing, it's hard to give those first five. But I think it is reflective -- I think if we were to take any five, this would be indicative of the amount of material for the five witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Well the correction, unless the Simatovic Defence would disagree with the corrections, we'll take the numbers as being corrected, but if, Mr. Bakrac, if you would disagree with the numbers now given by Mr. Groome, then of course we'd like to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I'm not in a position at all to disagree simply because I am completely and utterly new to the case, and the information concerned is information I received from members of the team of late Mr. Jovanovic who were unable to give me precise answers to my questions as to what sort of material this was, and the quantities involved. This was an approximation that we put into our motion. I do not doubt the sincerity of my learned friend, Mr. Groome. However, I believe that the correction which said that is it's not 5.000 pieces of evidence but 1.300 and -- or, rather, 3.548. And this is a case which is of the third degree of complexity, and the number of witnesses involved is already argumentation enough to support the points that is Mr. Petrovic and I placed in our motion. The case of such a complexity is prepared --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I asked you whether you wanted to give further questions to what Mr. Groome said. I do understand that you even feel not to be in a position to comment on that, and you slowly, I think, proceeded in -- well, emphasising what we find already in the motion to adjourn. And of course we'll read that, and we'll first weight what the response of the Prosecution to that will be. Nevertheless to be on a very practical level, if I would want to know how many documents there are on a 65 ter list, I would just look at that list. That would take me approximately three minutes to verify whether the number is correct or not, rather than asking others. I mean, that's all officially filed. You find it in e-court. So, therefore, I would be able to verify the numbers. And, well, if it would not be three minutes, then it would be four, but not anything more. But you have an opportunity to correct him, if what Mr. Groome said was not accurate. Any further matter in relation to these motions? Yes, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I'm not in a position to contradict Mr. Groome. I would like to recall that unfortunately late Mr. Jovanovic kept all the documentation with him. There is a procedure in place to get hold of the material. I haven't even met with Mr. Domazet to receive the material from him. As you are well aware, I was assigned as counsel on the 11th, on Friday, and this is the first working day. Hence, I'm not in a position to challenge any of the points put forth by Mr. Groome. Nevertheless, I don't think that the points we are trying to make in our motion is affected by this at all since the time necessary to prepare on all the material mentioned here does not change. I don't want to repeat everything that we've stated in our motion. I am at your disposal if the Trial Chamber would want me to clarify any of the points. But I don't want to repeat them all here, I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we find them in the writing. There's one matter I would like to briefly raise with you. I'm not asking for a response, but in the motion you, Mr. Bakrac, you are telling the Court that it will be a whole new team in every respect, not only counsel and co-counsel. First of all, I do not know whether this has already been approved by OLAD that others are replaced as well, but replacing all members of the team by others as a reason it to claim further time to prepare is not what the Chamber expects a responsible Defence team to do because work has been done by members of the team and profit, whatever profit can be taken from those who have worked on the case, that we can't just allow a team to throw that away and say, We need more time because we have a new team. Of course, unfortunately Mr. Jovanovic is not able to continue his job due to his, as you said also in the motion, his death, and therefore, under those circumstances, it's of utmost importance to keep everything and to carefully watch that nothing of the results by team members, up to that moment, will be lost. And replacing the whole team - the Chamber is aware of the position of Mr. Domazet who has been assigned to temporarily still assist the team - but to replace other team members might not be in the interests of judicial economy. And, therefore, I'm not going to further comment on it at this moment, but since it is announced that you need so much time also because the whole team will be new, that's not what the Chamber expects a team to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for not requiring me to reply right away, and thank you for allowing me to reply at a later stage after considering this matter. What I would like to state is that there is possibly a misunderstanding. As you can see, Ms. Ingrid Morgan is with me today. It wasn't until today that I received a full list of the team members. I had a meeting with OLAD before coming to this courtroom, and naturally I will do my best to use the services of every single team member who could contribute to speeding up the process. There is no need for me to go into further details right now, but I'm prepared to accept that any member of the team who can be of assistance to speed up the trial remain on the team. I wasn't able to meet and to talk with Mr. Domazet, who is our senior and esteemed colleague and who was co-counsel in this case, and I don't know to what extent he is prepared to continue as legal consultant in this case, given the relationship between him and my client. I'm not aware whether he is prepared or not. I'm certainly willing to take him on, but should that not be of assistance, then it would make more sense to take on board somebody else who would contribute to speeding up the trial. Otherwise, I fully agree with you that all resources that could be used in order to prepare for the case in a faster way needs to be done. And in all those cases where we think that a replacement would be useful, I will, regarding all those instances, submit a motion to you and to the Registrar concerning such situations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you are invited to further discuss the matter with OLAD, and I just wanted today express the concern of the Chamber where that language was used that the team would be replaced or there would be a wholly new team, that's not what we expected. Then Prosecution is invited to respond to the provisional release motion, if possible, together with the Stanisic provisional release motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will do that. And there is one matter that I would like to state and just to say it on the record, that I would request that Mr. Bakrac and Ms. Morgan come back to my office with me. I've arranged to have staff available to ensure that they have -- there are no disclosure issues, that they have access to all the disclosure material. And I'd like to begin that process today, so I just want to put on record that I'm requesting that they do return for a meeting with me, short meeting after this hearing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, you are invited for tea, Mr. Bakrac. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other matter to be raised at this moment? If not, the Chamber will issue -- once it has decided on the motions, will issue a Scheduling Order which of course will then be in accordance with the decision which will be -- by then, be delivered on the motion to adjourn. Therefore, we stand adjourned at this moment sine die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 2.50 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned sine die
